measured.critical_path:
Shape: `changes` (0.2) → about 25 parallel jobs → check (0.1). On develop, deploy-staging follows: preflight 0.1 → plan 0.6 → [migrate check + reviewer approval] → deploy 6.9 → release/ota 0.2.

Longest jobs by duration (median/p90 min), not counting queue:
PR: lint parity 10.9/13.7 > test mobile 8.6/12.2 > test api 6.3/9.2 > e2e shard 6.2/8.0 > verify lint 6.0/8.5 > test web 4.7/7.3.
Develop: lint parity 11.3/13.5 > e2e shard 8.9/11.3 (the phone project is added on pushes) > test mobile 8.8/11.6 > lint 7.5/9.2 > test api 7.3/9.2.

Last job to finish (attempt-1 runs; check and baselines excluded):
PR green (17): lint parity 11, test mobile 3, test api 2, e2e 1.
PR red (11): test mobile 5, lint parity 2, test api 2, lint 2.
Develop green (19): e2e shard 10, lint parity 4, test api 3, test mobile 2.

Queue on top of duration: a lone run fans out 25 jobs after `changes`, against an observed ceiling of 20 concurrent jobs. The plan lookup returned nothing; the peak observed across all sampled jobs was exactly 20, held 419 times. Runs with no other ci run overlapping:
- 16-job fan-out (no e2e): every job starts within 2-4 s.
- 25-job fan-out: the last job starts 42-345 s late.
With 2-4 overlapping runs the delay reaches 427-877 s. Live on 11-17 00:30, 3 PR runs and a develop push overlapped: develop run 43988092361 had jobs waiting up to 900 s, 205 job-minutes queued in total; PR run 43988066995 waited up to 810 s.

Supabase start: 72-80 s per shard (`time` output in shard logs 132999250849 / 133002683941; 255 migrations applied each time). It runs in the background, overlapped with the browser libraries and the build, so only 13-37 s (p90 43) of «Wait for local Supabase» lands on the path.
Per-shard overhead outside the test step: 114-117 s (p90 131).
Shard imbalance: the slowest shard takes about 2x the fastest (PR 372 vs 182 s; develop 579 vs 302 s, shard 2 the slowest). e2e/shard-durations.json was last changed 10-30.

Develop only: a push first waits for the previous develop run (p90 10.6 min). Then ci (13.5) + deploy (7-15) gives 27.3 min median merge to production. Inside the deploy, the VPS «Swap in and roll the API» step (316 s) is the longest.

Failure path: on a red lint, «Suppressions to prune» re-runs the whole turbo lint with --force, adding 389 s/486 s (7 PR runs) before the job ends. Oxlint's prune step adds 49 s.
measured.waste:
1. Develop re-runs what the PR already verified (log-proven). PR #743 ci 43774993150 replayed @ab/shared:build a0f04c78 and api:test e32c5729 as FULL TURBO in 6 s. Its merge push 43776097790 had the identical hashes but logged «cache miss, executing» and took 5m28s. On staff-mobile, 3 identical hashes (shared/client-core build, staff-mobile:test) also missed. Cause: rharkor/caching-for-turbo stores in the Actions cache, and entries saved on refs/pull/N/merge are not readable from refs/heads/develop. 4,649 of the 6,391 turbo entries sit on PR/branch refs. Turbo replay rate (main step under 30 s; typecheck excluded since it really runs in 12-26 s):
- PR: lint 28%, test api 32%, test web 48%, test mobile 33%, test others 47%.
- Develop: lint 5%, test api 5%, test web 10%, test mobile 10%.
So about 164 runner-minutes per merge, of which the verify share is already-verified work. A remote cache that is not scoped to a ref would remove it (e.g. TURBO_TOKEN, or a cache server on the VPS/MinIO).

2. Unrelated changes invalidate every test. 12 of the last 20 merged PRs edit packages/shared/i18n/ar.json/en.json (#743 was a family-app PR: 37 family-mobile files plus the 2 i18n files). That gives @ab/shared:build a new hash, and through `dependsOn: ^build` every api, web and staff-mobile test and lint task re-runs. A string edit re-runs the api unit tests.

3. The e2e spec selector never narrowed. 0 of 23 PR runs that ran e2e got a partial selection; each ran 8 shards + single line (about 47 runner-min, 41% of PR minutes). The «full suite» notice named:
- an apps/family-mobile/** file (incl. app.json): 10
- apps/family/app.json: 4
- apps/api/src/common/auth/parity/access-before.json: 5
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: 2
- the api import graph reaching app.module: 2
The `changes` diff regex itself treats family-mobile as e2e-irrelevant, but select.mjs counts it as unmapped, so the whole suite runs. Each notice gives one reason per run, so this shows the first unmapped file, not that the selection would otherwise have narrowed.

4. ESLint runs twice per run, never with --cache: verify lint 6.0-7.5 min, plus lint-parity «Parity with ESLint» 560 s/575 s median (p90 708). Parity is the last job in 11 of 17 green PR runs. Its full-repo ESLint (no suppressions, CONCURRENCY=3) is never replayed; parity.mjs already accepts LINT_PARITY_ESLINT=<findings.json> to reuse a saved run.

5. The runner ceiling is hit by the run itself. 28 jobs per full run against 20 slots. Small verify jobs each pay about 27 s of setup (checkout, pnpm, setup-node 11 s, pnpm i 9 s, turbo cache action):
- typecheck 0.8
- bundle family 1.1
- bundle mobile 1.2
- test family 1.4
- test others 1.7
- guards 2.1
Setup alone is about 11 runner-min per run, and these jobs occupy slots while e2e/test shards queue (queue p90 2-6 min on every job).

6. Cache budget overflow. The Actions cache holds 10.73 GB over the 10 GB limit (6,362 entries). Of that, 6.44 GB (60%) is 16 pnpm-store copies of 402 MB each ("node-cache-Linux-x64-pnpm-*" from setup-node `cache: pnpm`, one per lockfile hash per ref); only one (develop 854c2e…) was accessed on 11-17. vitest holds 179 entries / 1.88 GB, turbo 2.15 GB. As a result the oldest turbo last-access is 11-15 04:37: turbo entries are evicted after about 44 h.

7. Per-shard e2e setup repeated 9x: about 115 s each (≈17 runner-min per run).
- Supabase pull + start 72-80 s in the background, 255 migrations every shard.
- browser system libs installed from cached .debs 15 s (p90 23).
- build of e2e^... 10 s on PR / 37 s on develop (p90 56).
- setup-node + install 20 s.
The Playwright browser cache hit in 450 of 450 e2e jobs (no install).

8. Stale shard weights: shard-durations.json was last changed 10-30, and the per-run spread is 2x (develop shard 2 541 s vs shard 5 328 s). Rebalancing toward the mean (~430 s) would take about 2 min off develop's e2e path.

9. test mobile (jest-expo) runs on a single machine: 8.6/12.2 min, not sharded, last job in 8 of 28 PR runs.

10. Failure path: the lint prune step re-runs `turbo lint --force` (+389 s) inside the red job, so the red check arrives about 6.5 min later and holds a slot.

11. Cancelled/superseded runs: 13 of the 55 completed runs in the 60-run window (14 of 66 overall, 411 runner-min burned, median 0.4 min each). Six came from one burst on feat/chat-upgrade within 2 min (cheap). One PR run (43690194577, feat/biometric-login) was cancelled after 21 min, burning 134 runner-min. On develop, 2 queued pushes were replaced (by design). Develop pushes wait behind a running develop run (cancel-in-progress false): p90 10.6 min, max 14.3 (run 43692741211, 34.1 min wall).

12. Deploy: the API image is built on the VPS every deploy, inside the 316 s swap/roll step. The web build (46 s) and pnpm install repeat work ci just did. Overlapping deploys queue 3.5-5.6 min on the concurrency group.

Already working: docs-only runs skip verify (16 jobs); mobile-only PRs skip e2e (5 PR runs at 19 jobs); draft PRs skip e2e; typecheck replays 67-77%.

findings.title: Run lint parity off the verify-lint ESLint pass instead of a second full ESLint
findings.where: .github/workflows/ci.yml:122-220 (verify lint row) and 308-342 (lint-parity job); tools/scripts/ci-checks/lint/parity/parity.mjs:58-66 and eslint-run.mjs:16-57; turbo.json lint task (no outputs). Shape-pinning: tools/scripts/ci-checks/workflows-fast.test.mjs:45-58 (check.needs lists lint-parity); docs/31b and CLAUDE.md rule 3 name the «lint parity (oxlint)» job.
findings.minutes_saved: PR wall about -2 min median and -2 to -3 min p90. Parity is the last job in 11 of 17 green PR runs at 10.9/13.7. The merged lint row would take about 6.0 + 1.2 (oxfull) + 1.7 (compare and config parity) = ~9 min, which leaves test mobile 8.6/12.2 and test api 6.3/9.2 next in line. Develop: parity (11.3) drops out and the lint row becomes ~10.5, so ~0-1 min unless F3 also lands. Slots: one fewer job and ~8 runner-min less per run, because the 533.5 s ESLint pass in job 133727128957 is gone.
findings.change: ESLint already produces what parity needs. With bulk suppressions applied, ESLint 10.11 moves suppressed messages into suppressedMessages tagged suppressions [{kind:'file'}] (lib/services/suppressions-service.js:275-296), and the JSON output keeps them. messages plus the file-kind suppressedMessages therefore equal parity's 'no suppressions' run. Inline eslint-disable stays kind 'directive' in both runs. Steps: (1) Add a small ESLint formatter in packages/config. It writes that JSON to <pkg>/.lint/eslint.json and returns stylish text, so the log stays readable. Pass it through `pnpm turbo lint ... -- -f <formatter>`. (2) In turbo.json, give lint outputs ['.lint/**'] and list the formatter file as an input, so a replayed package restores its findings. (3) After turbo lint, the lint row runs `pnpm lint:oxfull` and then `pnpm lint:parity`, with parity reading those files. LINT_PARITY_ESLINT already exists; extend it to a folder, and as a fail-safe lint only the packages that have no file. (4) Delete the lint-parity job, remove it from check.needs, and move its two failure steps (the oxlint prune diff and the report artifact) into the lint row.
findings.risk: Low-medium. Coverage does not change (same config, same files), but the proof now depends on reading suppressedMessages correctly. Add a unit test showing that a file-suppressed finding still counts as missing when Oxlint lacks it. The comment at parity.mjs:62 says 'CI runs it', and the job summary loses the separate ESLint wall time; print turbo's lint time instead. Turbo entries saved before the outputs change have no .lint file; the fail-safe re-lints those packages. The lint row grows to ~9/11.5 min, inside its 20-min timeout. workflows-fast.test.mjs, docs/31b and the CLAUDE.md line that names the CI job need editing in the same PR.

findings.title: Parity runs type-aware Oxlint a second time, right after «Oxlint (every rule)»
findings.where: tools/scripts/ci-checks/lint/parity/parity.mjs:61 calls runOxlint(root) again, although tools/scripts/ci-checks/lint/oxlint/run.mjs:44-48 wrote oxlint-report.json one step earlier (ci.yml:325-329).
findings.minutes_saved: -1.2 min on the lint-parity job: the two Oxlint runs in job 133727128957 took 73.7 s and 72.5 s back to back. That is PR wall time whenever parity is the last job (11 of 17 green PR runs). F1 covers it, but this is a few lines and can ship first.
findings.change: Have parity.mjs read oxlint-report.json when ci.yml says so (for example LINT_PARITY_OXLINT=oxlint-report.json, set on the Parity step), and otherwise run Oxlint as today.
findings.risk: Very low. Both runs use the same binary, config and arguments (ARGS in run.mjs). The summary still shows the Oxlint time printed by the first step.

findings.title: Develop: skip verify, guards and lint parity when a green PR run already tested the exact tree
findings.where: ci.yml:35-108 (changes); 122-126, 257-259 and 308-311 (job ifs); 350-379 (baselines has needs: guards); 384-405 (check). Shape-pinning: workflows.test.mjs:45-58 (baselines.needs === 'guards' and its if), workflows-fast.test.mjs:45-58 (check.needs and its shell).
findings.minutes_saved: On qualifying pushes, develop wall drops from 13.5 to ~10.5 min median, because e2e (slowest shard 8.9/11.3) becomes the whole run; ~9.5 with F4. Merge-to-production improves by 2-3 min, and the wait behind the previous develop run (p90 10.6 min) shrinks with it. Each qualifying merge runs 16 fewer jobs and ~85 fewer runner-min (164 → ~80), which PR runs feel as shorter queues. About 21 of 29 recent develop pushes would qualify. That count comes from timestamps (the PR's last green ci run started after the parent commit landed on develop). Only #743 is hash-proven: PR run 43774993150 and push run 43776097790 computed the same task hashes.
findings.change: PR side: `changes` outputs `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` for the merge commit it checked out. When verify, guards and lint-parity all succeeded (not on the docs-only path), `check` uploads a one-line artifact named ci-green-tree-<tree> with retention-days 7. Push side: `changes` computes HEAD^{tree} and calls GET /actions/artifacts?name=ci-green-tree-<tree> (it already has actions: read). A match whose workflow_run.head_repository_id is this repo sets verified=true. verify, guards and lint-parity add `&& needs.changes.outputs.verified != 'true'`, and check accepts them as skipped when verified=true. e2e stays as it is (full suite, both projects). baselines becomes needs [changes, guards] with always(), and runs when guards succeeded or verified=true, since it re-runs knip and queries itself. Fail-safe: an API error or no match means everything runs. Leave develop's cancel-in-progress alone (ci.yml:17-21); cancelling a running develop run changes what ships, and a shorter run fixes the wait anyway.
findings.risk: Low-medium. The tree includes ci.yml, so a forged artifact can only match a tree whose ci.yml already ran on develop. There are two real costs. (1) Skipped develop pushes stop writing turbo and vitest entries on the default branch, the only cache scope every PR can read, so a PR's first run may replay less. This is unmeasured; F13 avoids it. (2) Flaky or clock-dependent unit tests no longer get a second run on develop. Update the two tests named in 'where' in the same PR.

findings.title: Refresh e2e shard weights from the newest develop run, and widen develop e2e once F3 frees slots
findings.where: ci.yml:538-555 («Shard sizes»); e2e/shard-durations.json (last changed 10-30; 179 entries for 204 spec files); `merge` mode in tools/scripts/ci-checks/e2e-shards.mjs (already exists); the 8-shard fallback matrix at ci.yml:432, used by every push; MAX_SHARDS in e2e-areas/plan.mjs (PRs only). Shape-pinning: plan.test.mjs, single-line.test.mjs, workflows-fast.test.mjs:85.
findings.minutes_saved: Develop wall and merge-to-production improve by about 2 min. In develop run 43988092361 the measured spec time per shard ranged from 238 to 467 s (mean 328), while the committed weights predicted 205-306 s; shard 2 was off by 167 s. Balanced cuts should bring the slowest shard to about 340-350 s. e2e is the last job in 10 of 19 green develop runs. On PRs the slowest shard gains ~1 min, but it is rarely on the path. Optional after F3: 12 develop shards (2620 s / 12 ≈ 220 s of specs each) would save another 1.5-2 min for ~13 more runner-min.
findings.change: In «Shard sizes», download the e2e-durations-push-* artifacts of the newest successful develop ci run (gh run download, actions: read), merge them with `e2e-shards.mjs merge`, and compute the weights from that file. On any error, fall back to the committed file. Alternatively, do this once in `changes` and pass the file (~10 KB) to the shards as an output. For 12 develop shards, change only the push fallback at ci.yml:432, and only after F3 has freed the slots.
findings.risk: Low. Playwright still runs every test once; only the cut points move. Moving the cuts gives specs new neighbours on a shard's single database, which can expose an order-dependent spec (e2e-shards.mjs says so in its own comment). Artifacts older than 14 days have expired, and the step then falls back to the committed file. 12 shards add four Supabase stacks to each develop run, so pair that step with F3.

findings.title: e2e spec selection: family-mobile, mobile-kit and an API test fixture force the full suite
findings.where: tools/scripts/ci-checks/e2e-areas/select.mjs:16 (NO_E2E lists apps/staff-mobile only, while ci.yml:74 also exempts apps/family-mobile and packages/mobile-kit); select.mjs:24 (UNIT); select.mjs:91-96 (bundleUsers reads only apps/staff-mobile as a mobile key reader); ci.yml:107 (the notice prints a single reason). Tests: select.test.mjs, i18n.test.mjs.
findings.minutes_saved: These paths were the first full-suite reason in at most 19 of 23 PR e2e runs: family-mobile 10, apps/family 4 (the old path, now apps/family-mobile), access-before.json 5. The same PRs often carry other full-suite triggers (packages/mobile-kit/src is outside GRAPHED, plus package.json, the lockfile and migrations), so the real hit rate stays unknown until the notice lists every reason. Each narrowed run drops from 9 e2e machines to 2-4 and saves ~30-40 runner-min. Its fan-out shrinks from 25 jobs toward 16-19, under the observed 20-job ceiling. Lone 16-job runs started every job within 2-4 s, while lone 25-job runs started their last job 42-345 s late, so PR wall drops by 1-4 min on those runs.
findings.change: Add ^apps/family-mobile/ and ^packages/mobile-kit/ to NO_E2E. In bundleUsers, read apps/family-mobile and packages/mobile-kit as mobile key readers (ignored like staff-mobile), so a key that only the family app reads is known instead of failing with 'no reader found'. Add ^apps/api/src/common/auth/parity/ to UNIT; access-before.json is read only by permissions.parity.test.ts and route-walk.test-util.ts. Make select.mjs collect and print every full-suite reason, so the next measurement shows the real hit rate.
findings.risk: Low. Develop pushes still run the full suite on both projects, which catches a spec the selection missed. A family PR that also changes an API module still selects that module's areas through the import graph. Confirm that staff-web imports nothing from packages/mobile-kit; ci.yml:24-26 already relies on that.

findings.title: Shard the staff-mobile jest run and keep its transform cache
findings.where: ci.yml:142 (a single `test mobile` row); packages/mobile-kit/jest.base.cjs sets no cacheDirectory, so jest uses its default temp directory, which disappears with the runner. Shape-pinning: mobile-family.test.mjs:73-79 (row names and filters).
findings.minutes_saved: test mobile takes 8.6/12.2 min (jest ran 1057 suites in 474.9 s in job 133727129362). Two shards should bring it to about 5/7. The transform cache adds an unmeasured upside; the log does not split transform time from run time. test mobile was the last job in 8 of 28 PR runs (5 of the 11 red ones), and after F1 it sets the PR p90. PR wall: about -1 to -3 min at p90. Cost: one more job (~30 s of setup).
findings.change: Replace the row with `test mobile 1/2` and `test mobile 2/2`, using args '-- --shard=1/2' and '-- --shard=2/2' (check the pinned jest version's docs for --shard). In CI, set cacheDirectory to '<rootDir>/node_modules/.jest-cache' and restore and save it like the vitest cache: key on the lockfile, babel.config.cjs, the jest configs and the shard; save on develop, or when nothing was restored.
findings.risk: Low. The jest cache holds transforms keyed by file content and config, never results, so every test still runs. Shards split by test file path and may come out uneven; compare the two times after a week. This adds one job to a fan-out that is already over 20.

findings.title: Build the API image on the VPS while ci runs, so the deploy only rolls
findings.where: deploy-staging.yml:276-313 (ship, then «Swap in and roll», 316 s/383 s); deploy/staging/roll.sh:79 (`dc build ayat-worker` on every deploy). Shape-pinning: roll.test.mjs, rollback.test.mjs, compose/compose-roll.test.mjs, workflows.test.mjs:104-119 (secrets only in environment-bound jobs) and :139 (docs table of secrets and environments).
findings.minutes_saved: Merge-to-production about -4 min. In deploy run 43815028836 the image build took ~250 s of the roll step: context 12 s, COPY 11.5 s, install plus build 139 s, browser plus apt 47 s, export plus unpack 59 s. The roll itself took ~60 s. The develop ci run lasts 10-13 min, so a build started at push time finishes before deploy-staging begins. The build also leaves the deploy path on the box that hosts the live CRM.
findings.change: Add a small workflow that runs on push to develop (environment develop, the same SSH secrets as deploy). It ships `git archive` to $DEST/src.<sha> and runs `docker compose build`, tagging the image ayat-api:<sha>; it never touches running containers. Give roll.sh an image argument: when ayat-api:<sha> exists it rolls that image, otherwise it builds as today. Prune ayat-api:<sha> tags older than the last two deploys.
findings.risk: Medium. A second workflow holds the deploy key; it is environment-bound and push-only, so workflows.test.mjs:104 stays green. A build for a commit that later fails ci is discarded, the VPS spends the CPU either way, and two quick pushes build twice. The roll.sh and rollback.sh tests pin the current single-build flow. The alternative is to build in GitHub and push to GHCR, which puts registry credentials on the VPS and adds a ~1 GB pull to every deploy.

findings.title: API Dockerfile: the browser/apt layer and pnpm install re-run on every deploy
findings.where: apps/api/Dockerfile:10-13 (`COPY . .` then a cold `pnpm install`; the log shows 'reused 0' and 59 s); Dockerfile:18 vs :29 (COPY --from=build /repo comes before the playwright + apt RUN, so that 47 s layer never hits the cache). Shape-pinning: builds/workspace-builds.test.mjs:14-16 (searches for the literal 'RUN pnpm install'), compose/compose-pdf.test.mjs:64-65.
findings.minutes_saved: About -1.5 min per deploy and merge-to-production: ~47 s from the browser/apt layer plus ~45 s of the 56 s install. Less after F7 takes the build off the path.
findings.change: In stage 2, install chromium-shell and the apt packages before `COPY --from=build`, passing the playwright-core version as a build arg read from pnpm-lock.yaml. After the COPY, assert that /repo/apps/api/node_modules/playwright-core has that version. Run the install as `RUN --mount=type=cache,id=ayat-pnpm,target=<pnpm store> pnpm install ...`, or add a `pnpm fetch` layer built from the lockfile alone. Optionally use `pnpm deploy --prod` to cut the 59 s export.
findings.risk: Low-medium. A browser built for another playwright-core version breaks the PDF render, which is why the version check matters. roll.sh notes that the BuildKit cache is shared with the CRM, so the pnpm cache mount grows there; prune it by id. A --mount prefix breaks the literal 'RUN pnpm install' search in workspace-builds.test.mjs.

findings.title: Raise the concurrent-job ceiling (an account plan setting, no workflow change)
findings.where: The AhmedAmiin0 personal account plan (public repo). `gh api user` returns plan: null; the 20-job ceiling is an observation (peak of exactly 20, held 419 times in the sample).
findings.minutes_saved: Queue p90 is 2-6 min on every job. With 2-4 overlapping runs the last job waited 427-877 s, and one live snapshot held 205 queued job-minutes. Lone 25-job runs start their last job 42-345 s late. If GitHub's documented limits still hold (40 concurrent jobs on Pro, 20 on Free), p90 for PR and develop runs could drop by 3-5 min and the median by 0.5-1 min.
findings.change: Owner decision: move the account to GitHub Pro. I changed no settings. Check GitHub's current price and concurrency limits before deciding.
findings.risk: No technical risk, only a monthly cost. Confirm the current plan on the billing page first, because the ceiling was inferred from job timings.

findings.title: Fold the small verify rows into two
findings.where: ci.yml:134 (typecheck, 0.8 min), 145-149 (test family 1.4, test others 1.7), 152-153 (bundle mobile 1.2, bundle family 1.1). Shape-pinning: mobile-bundle.test.mjs:14-18, mobile-family.test.mjs:73-79.
findings.minutes_saved: 3 fewer jobs per full run (28 → 25) and ~1.5 runner-min of setup (~27 s per job). Not on the path by itself; together with F5 it keeps more runs under the 20-job ceiling.
findings.change: Replace typecheck, bundle mobile and bundle family with one `typecheck + bundles` row running `pnpm turbo typecheck bundle`; only the two Expo apps have a bundle task, so turbo runs every typecheck and both Metro bundles in one graph. Merge test family into `test others` by removing the family-mobile and @ab/mobile-kit exclusions from its filter.
findings.risk: Low. The merged rows take ~2 min and ~2.5-5 min, well short of the path. When a merged row goes red, you have to read the log to see which part failed. The two test files pin the row names and filters.

findings.title: Build the web app in its own deploy-staging job while plan and migrate run
findings.where: deploy-staging.yml:184-205 (setup-node, pnpm i, the staff-web^... build and the staff-web build all run inside «deploy»).
findings.minutes_saved: Deploy and merge-to-production about -1 min: setup-node ~11 s, install ~10 s, build 46 s/72 s. It becomes a larger share of the deploy once F7 lands.
findings.change: Add a `web` job with needs: preflight and environment develop (the same VITE_* values). It builds apps/staff-web/dist and uploads it as an artifact. «deploy» gets needs [preflight, migrate, web] and downloads the artifact instead of building.
findings.risk: Low. The artifact stays inside the run. Runs where a migration waits for the reviewer gain nothing. deploy's if must also check web's result.

findings.title: Red lint: run the prune only when ESLint reports stale suppressions
findings.where: ci.yml:214-220 («Suppressions to prune» runs `pnpm lint:prune`, which is `turbo lint --force` over every package; see package.json). Shape-pinning: workflows-fast.test.mjs:79-83.
findings.minutes_saved: When the failure is a real violation, the red check arrives up to 6.5 min sooner (the prune took 389 s/486 s in 7 PR runs) and the runner frees sooner. When suppressions are stale, limiting the prune to the failing packages cuts it to their own lint time (1-3 min).
findings.change: Tee the turbo lint output to a file. Run the prune only if the output contains ESLint's 'There are suppressions left that do not occur anymore' message, and limit it with --filter to the packages that printed it (turbo prefixes each line with the package name).
findings.risk: Low. If detection misses a case, the log lacks the prune diff, but the job is red either way. Update the regex in workflows-fast.test.mjs.

findings.title: Alternative to F3: a turbo cache that is not scoped to a git ref
findings.where: ci.yml:165-166, 322-323, 528-529 (rharkor/caching-for-turbo) and the comment at ci.yml:116-118. workflows.test.mjs:104-119 forbids workflow-level secrets and secrets in jobs without an environment, and its comment at :111 records 'no TURBO_TOKEN (2026-10-30)'.
findings.minutes_saved: Little wall time on its own. Develop verify rows would replay in ~1 min each, but lint parity (a plain node script, never replayed, 11.3 min) and the slowest e2e shard (~11 min) would still finish last. The gain is freed runner slots: ~60-70 runner-min per merge, PRs replaying each other's tasks, and 2.15 GB leaving the Actions cache. Not additive with F3, but it avoids F3's cost of develop no longer writing default-branch cache entries.
findings.change: Owner decision. Run a cache server (for example ducktors/turborepo-remote-cache backed by the existing MinIO) or use Vercel Remote Cache. Replace the rharkor step with TURBO_API, TURBO_TEAM and TURBO_TOKEN, and set TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY.
findings.risk: Medium, and it goes against a recorded decision. PR runs would need a token; the repo is public, and fork PRs get no secret, so they fall back to the local cache. A self-hosted server adds a public endpoint on the VPS that runs the live CRM. A same-repo PR could write a cache entry that replays green on develop; deploy builds do not use the turbo cache, so shipped code is unaffected. It needs either an environment-bound job design or a change to workflows.test.mjs.

findings.title: Stop saving a 402 MB pnpm store per PR ref
findings.where: setup-node `cache: pnpm` in ci.yml (verify, guards, lint-parity, baselines, e2e), deploy-staging.yml, mobile.yml and db-migrate.yml. The Actions cache holds 10.73 GB against a 10 GB limit, 6.44 GB of it in 16 node-cache-Linux-x64-pnpm-* copies, and the oldest turbo entry is only ~44 h old.
findings.minutes_saved: Indirect. Freeing ~5.6 GB lets turbo and vitest entries outlive the ~44 h eviction, so PRs on older bases replay more (unmeasured, perhaps 0.5-2 min per such PR run). A PR that changes the lockfile would restore the previous store through a prefix key instead of starting cold (unmeasured).
findings.change: Replace `cache: pnpm` with actions/cache/restore on the pnpm store path (key pnpm-store-<lockfile hash>, restore-keys pnpm-store-) in every job, and save it with actions/cache/save from a single develop job when the key missed. In the same PR, have develop save the vitest cache only when the lockfile or config part of the restored key differs, instead of 8 new run-id keys per run (179 entries, 1.88 GB).
findings.risk: Low. The first PR after a lockfile change downloads its new packages from the network. Before relying on setup-node's save behaviour, read its action.yml at the pinned v4 tag; the evidence here is the per-ref copies in the cache listing.

findings.title: API unit tests spend 92% of their time importing modules: try the threads pool
findings.where: apps/api/vitest.config.mts sets no pool and no isolate option. Job 133727129366, shard 1/3: 'Duration 503.50s (import 92%, tests 6%, transform 2%)'.
findings.minutes_saved: Unknown until measured. test api uses 15% of runner-minutes at 6.3/9.2 min per shard; if import time halved, each shard would save ~3 min.
findings.change: Open an experiment PR that sets `pool: 'threads'` in the api vitest config, then compare the three shard times and the flake rate over a few runs. Keep per-file isolation on. First read the pinned vitest version's docs for its default pool.
findings.risk: Medium. Nest tests compiled with swc may behave differently in worker threads than in forks (process globals, native modules). isolate: false would cut import time the most, but it shares module state across files and can leak vi.mock; do not ship that.

findings.title: i18n edits that invalidate every task: little to gain
findings.where: turbo.json build inputs: $TURBO_DEFAULT$ includes packages/shared/i18n/*.json, although tsconfig.build.json compiles only src. Non-test readers of the bundles: api (2 files), staff-web (6), staff-mobile (6), mobile-kit (1), e2e (7), tools/migrate, tools/scripts. Shape-pinning: turbo-inputs.test.mjs.
findings.minutes_saved: ~0 on the critical path. Excluding i18n/** from @ab/shared#build would spare only client-core, family-mobile and the small packages, because api, staff-web, staff-mobile and e2e read the bundles and would have to list them as inputs.
findings.change: Skip this, or do it only if the same PR adds the bundles to the task inputs of every reader. Re-running the api tests after a string edit is correct today: server-text.ts and config-seeder.ts read ar.json.
findings.risk: A wrong reader list replays a stale green test, and the small gain does not justify that risk.

findings.title: Combined projection and what already works
findings.where: All findings above. Data: 66 ci runs (11-14 to 11-17), plus single-log samples from jobs 133727128957, 133727129362 and 133727129366 and deploy run 43815028836.
findings.minutes_saved: PR whole run: 12.7/17.7 → ~10.5/14.5 with F1, F2, F5, F6 and F10 (lint at ~9 min, then test api's 9.2 p90, set the path); ~10/12 with F9 as well. Develop: 13.5/23.1 → ~9.5-10/12 on qualifying pushes with F3 and F4 (e2e alone). Merge-to-production: 27.3 → ~18-19 min with F3, F4, F7, F8 and F11. Runs with a migration still wait for the reviewer; that 63 min stays.
findings.change: Suggested order: F2 and F5 (small diffs), then F1, F4, F3 and F6, then the deploy work: F8, F11, F7. F9 is the owner's call at any time; F13 only if the owner reverses the no-token decision. Already working, no change needed: Claude Code Review skips drafts and is never on the path (0.7 min); the Playwright browser cache hit in 450 of 450 jobs; Supabase starts in the background with only 13-37 s on the path (an earlier measurement found caching its images slower than pulling them); docs-only and mobile-only PRs skip their heavy jobs; superseded PR pushes are already cancelled.
findings.risk: The savings are mostly not additive: each fix moves the last-finishing job to the next one, so read the projections as estimates. Every gate stays: lint (ESLint plus the oxlint parity check), typecheck, unit tests, guards, full e2e on develop with both projects, Claude review, and the migration reviewer.
